snippet.title: What If You Fell Into Quicksand? 🏜️
snippet.description:
You step into quicksand. You pull. You yell. Your friend pulls. Your arm files a complaint. 🙃 Turns out everything the movies taught you makes it worse… and the real escape is basically a lazy Sunday in a pool.

FACT CHECK
• Quicksand is sand saturated with water (often with clay). When you move, it liquefies around you and you sink; when you stay still, the sand settles and packs tightly around your legs.
• Bonn et al., Nature 434, 1079 (2005), "Quicksand and the human body": quicksand is about twice as dense as the human body (~2 g/ml vs ~1 g/ml), so you can't be sucked under; you sink only to about your waist and then float.
• The same study estimates that pulling a foot out at 1 cm/s needs a force of about 10^6 newtons, comparable to lifting a medium-sized car.
• The way out: stop struggling, lean back to spread your weight, and wiggle your legs slowly so water flows back into the packed sand and loosens it.
